Curriculum

Three levels, one clear path

Each level is 10 to 12 weeks with one 60-minute session a week, so the whole course takes 30 to 36 weeks. Every level has the same rhythm and ends with a project you design, build and show.

Week 6: friendly checkpointWeeks 10 and 11: final projectWeek 12: showcase and exit check

In a 10-week plan, two pairs of weeks are combined. Holiday weeks without a session do not count. Weeks 1 to 5 bring new ideas, week 6 is a review, weeks 7 to 9 bring more new ideas, and the last weeks are for the project.

Level 1

Introduction

Scratch 3 offline app (no account) for weeks 1–6; Thonny with Python's built-in turtle for weeks 7–12.

What students learn

  • write precise step-by-step instructions (algorithms) and put them in the right order
  • use loops to repeat actions and make patterns
  • use events and conditionals to make programs react
  • use variables (score, size, answers) and random numbers
  • break a problem into parts and make reusable blocks/functions
  • find and fix bugs using a strategy
  • work in a pair (driver/navigator) and explain their code
  • stay safe and fair online: privacy, credit, kindness, accessible design
  • read and write simple text-based Python programs in Thonny

Final project: My Interactive Art Show

(Python turtle). The program greets the viewer, asks 1–2 questions (input), and draws a scene or pattern using at least: a loop, a variable, an if, random, and at least one function made with def. Support path: Scratch version with the same rubric. Extension path: add key presses (onkey).

Open Level 1

Level 2

Intermediate

Thonny, Python 3.10+ standard library only (turtle, random, time, files). pytest (installed once via Thonny's package manager) from week 8.

What students learn

  • use clearly named variables of different types (int, float, str, bool) and f-strings
  • combine control structures: while loops, nested loops, compound conditions
  • write functions with parameters and return values to organize code
  • store and process collections with lists and dictionaries
  • read and write text files to save and load data
  • debug systematically (read tracebacks, print-debugging, rubber duck) and write simple tests
  • build event-driven games and generative art with turtle
  • plan with pseudocode/flowcharts, work in a team and act on feedback
  • make safe, fair, private choices about data and media

Final project: Arcade Game or Art Studio

Choose: (a) an arcade game in turtle with keys + timer + score, or (b) a generative art studio that saves/loads designs. Must use: functions with parameters/returns, a list, a dictionary, a while or game loop/timer, a file (high scores or saved art), and at least 3 pytest tests of their own functions.

Open Level 2

Level 3

Advanced

Thonny (or any editor), Terminal for git (Apple's free Command Line Tools; no GitHub account), Python standard library only (turtle, csv, random, collections, json), pytest.

What students learn

  • design programs with classes, objects, inheritance and composition
  • explain and compare searching/sorting algorithms and use recursion
  • choose data structures: lists of objects, dicts, stacks, queues, 2D grids
  • track their work with git (init, add, commit, log, diff, restore)
  • plan and build a larger program iteratively, using feedback
  • collect, clean, analyze and visualize data
  • explain how simple AI learns from data and where it fails
  • test and debug larger programs
  • reason about privacy, bias, ethics and licenses

Final project: Build Something Big

Choose: (a) a grid game, (b) a generative art app, or (c) a data/AI app. Must use: at least 2 classes (one using inheritance or composition), a data structure beyond a flat list (dict, stack/queue or grid), one named algorithm (search/sort/recursion/BFS), a saved file, at least 5 pytest tests, and a git history with 8+ meaningful commits.

Open Level 3

How progress is measured

Through projects, rubrics and friendly checkpoints, never grades. Rubrics have four levels: Just starting, Getting there, Got it and Expert. Creativity, working code and the ability to explain it count equally.

Parents: see how progress is checked and what the research says.

Kids Coding

A free course for children from Grade 5: make games and art, first with Scratch blocks, then with Python. One 60-minute session a week.

No accounts, no ads, no tracking.
